benediction.title: Benediction of the Most Blessed Sacrament
benediction.intro: The usual order of Benediction: the Blessed Sacrament is exposed while O Salutaris is sung; other approved hymns, a litany or prayers may follow; the Tantum Ergo is sung with incensation, followed by the versicle and prayer; the priest blesses the people with the monstrance in silence; the Divine Praises are said; and the Adoremus with Psalm 116 is sung as the Sacrament is reposed. Local customs vary.
benediction.source: Latin hymns: St. Thomas Aquinas (Verbum supernum and Pange lingua, 13th century). English hymn versions: Edward Caswall (1849, public domain). Divine Praises: as in use in 1960. Psalm 116: Douay-Rheims.
benediction.review: Needs review against a printed manual of prayers.

items.la:
O salutaris Hostia,
Quae caeli pandis ostium:
Bella premunt hostilia,
Da robur, fer auxilium.

Uni trinoque Domino
Sit sempiterna gloria,
Qui vitam sine termino
Nobis donet in patria. Amen.

items.r: All bow at the first lines; the priest incenses the Blessed Sacrament.
items.la:
Tantum ergo Sacramentum
Veneremur cernui:
Et antiquum documentum
Novo cedat ritui:
Praestet fides supplementum
Sensuum defectui.

Genitori, Genitoque
Laus et iubilatio,
Salus, honor, virtus quoque
Sit et benedictio:
Procedenti ab utroque
Compar sit laudatio. Amen.
items.en:
Down in adoration falling,
Lo! the sacred Host we hail;
Lo! o'er ancient forms departing,
Newer rites of grace prevail;
Faith for all defects supplying,
Where the feeble senses fail.

To the everlasting Father,
And the Son who reigns on high,
With the Holy Ghost proceeding
Forth from each eternally,
Be salvation, honour, blessing,
Might and endless majesty. Amen.

items.r: In Eastertide and within the octave of Corpus Christi, Alleluia is added to the versicle and response.
items.la:
V. Panem de caelo praestitisti eis.
R. Omne delectamentum in se habentem.

Oremus. Deus, qui nobis sub Sacramento mirabili passionis tuae memoriam reliquisti: tribue, quaesumus, ita nos corporis et sanguinis tui sacra mysteria venerari, ut redemptionis tuae fructum in nobis iugiter sentiamus. Qui vivis et regnas in saecula saeculorum.
R. Amen.
items.en:
V. Thou didst give them bread from heaven.
R. Containing in itself all sweetness.

Let us pray. O God, Who under a wonderful Sacrament hast left us a memorial of Thy Passion: grant us, we beseech Thee, so to venerate the sacred mysteries of Thy Body and Blood, that we may ever feel within us the fruit of Thy redemption. Who livest and reignest world without end.
R. Amen.

items.r: The priest makes the Sign of the Cross over the people with the monstrance, in silence. All kneel and bow.
Said after the blessing. This is the form as it stood in 1960 (the Precious Blood was added that year); the invocation of the Holy Ghost, the Paraclete, was added in 1964.
items.la:
Benedictus Deus.
Benedictum Nomen Sanctum eius.
Benedictus Iesus Christus, verus Deus et verus homo.
Benedictum Nomen Iesu.
Benedictum Cor eius sacratissimum.
Benedictus Sanguis eius pretiosissimus.
Benedictus Iesus in sanctissimo altaris Sacramento.
Benedicta excelsa Mater Dei, Maria sanctissima.
Benedicta sancta eius et immaculata Conceptio.
Benedicta eius gloriosa Assumptio.
Benedictum nomen Mariae, Virginis et Matris.
Benedictus sanctus Ioseph, eius castissimus Sponsus.
Benedictus Deus in Angelis suis, et in Sanctis suis.
items.en:
Blessed be God.
Blessed be His holy Name.
Blessed be Jesus Christ, true God and true Man.
Blessed be the Name of Jesus.
Blessed be His most Sacred Heart.
Blessed be His most Precious Blood.
Blessed be Jesus in the most holy Sacrament of the Altar.
Blessed be the great Mother of God, Mary most holy.
Blessed be her holy and Immaculate Conception.
Blessed be her glorious Assumption.
Blessed be the name of Mary, Virgin and Mother.
Blessed be Saint Joseph, her most chaste spouse.
Blessed be God in His Angels and in His Saints.

items.r: Sung as the Blessed Sacrament is replaced in the tabernacle.
items.la:
Adoremus in aeternum sanctissimum Sacramentum.

Laudate Dominum, omnes gentes: laudate eum, omnes populi.
Quoniam confirmata est super nos misericordia eius: et veritas Domini manet in aeternum.
Gloria Patri, et Filio, et Spiritui Sancto. Sicut erat in principio, et nunc, et semper, et in saecula saeculorum. Amen.

Adoremus in aeternum sanctissimum Sacramentum.
items.en:
Let us adore for ever the most holy Sacrament.

O praise the Lord, all ye nations: praise Him, all ye people.
For His mercy is confirmed upon us: and the truth of the Lord remaineth for ever.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

Let us adore for ever the most holy Sacrament.

home.title: Blessing of Homes on the Epiphany
home.intro: The Roman Ritual gives a blessing of homes on the feast of the Epiphany. It belongs to the priest; where a priest cannot come, families have long kept the custom of praying together and marking the lintel of the door in chalk with the year and the initials of the Magi, for example 20 ✠ C ✠ M ✠ B ✠ 27. The letters are also read as Christus mansionem benedicat, “May Christ bless this house.”
home.source: Rituale Romanum, Benedictio domorum in festo Epiphaniae. Psalm 71: Douay-Rheims.
home.review: Needs review against a printed Rituale Romanum; only the closing prayer of the rite is given here.

items.la: Ab Oriente venerunt Magi in Bethlehem adorare Dominum: et apertis thesauris suis pretiosa munera obtulerunt: aurum sicut regi magno, thus sicut Deo vero, myrrham sepulturae eius, alleluia.
items.en: From the East came the Magi to Bethlehem to adore the Lord; and opening their treasures, they offered precious gifts: gold to the great King, frankincense to the true God, and myrrh in symbol of His burial. Alleluia.

items.r: Said by the priest, who sprinkles the rooms with holy water.
items.la:
Oremus. Benedic, ✠ Domine Deus omnipotens, domum istam: ut sit in ea sanitas, castitas, victoriae virtus, humilitas, bonitas et mansuetudo, plenitudo legis, et gratiarum actio Deo Patri, et Filio, et Spiritui Sancto; et haec benedictio maneat super hanc domum, et super habitantes in ea. Per Christum Dominum nostrum.
R. Amen.
items.en:
Let us pray. Bless, ✠ O Lord God almighty, this home, that in it there may be health, purity, the strength of victory, humility, goodness and mildness, the fulness of the law, and thanksgiving to God the Father, Son, and Holy Ghost; and may this blessing remain upon this home and upon all who dwell herein. Through Christ our Lord.
R. Amen.
